findings.claim: utf8::decode($text) silently leaves the text as raw bytes when the frontmatter is not valid UTF-8. The following /u regexes then treat a stray 0x85 or 0xA0 byte as the Unicode characters U+0085 or U+00A0 and trim them, whereas Go's strings.TrimSpace does not trim those bytes in invalid UTF-8. utf8::encode($project) then double-encodes any high bytes in the project name. The rehearsal can therefore report a project value that differs from the one the command reads, or one whose bytes are corrupted. The failure needs a page with invalid UTF-8 in its frontmatter, which is rare but not excluded.

evidence: Checked the index arithmetic of the new readable test: the closing rule starts at offset $close+4 in $raw, which equals the first "---\n" found from offset 4, so the empty-frontmatter case and the normal case classify as intended.
Checked the project parsing against the Go behavior the comments describe (trim, first colon, skip empty and [], strip double quotes only); it matches for valid UTF-8.
The one divergence found is the handling of invalid UTF-8 input, reported as F1.
